canonical_claim: The return on the average actively managed dollar equals the market return before costs.
recommended_action: Record as a single derived claim with its premises attached; do not count the four units as independent corroboration.
synthesis: Four units agree, but they are one deductive chain rather than four observations: the market return is a weighted average of its constituents (0007), each passive manager receives it (0008), and the average active dollar is therefore the residual (0009, restated in 0001). The agreement is entailment, so it carries the weight of one argument. Its force rests entirely on the definition of passive holding in 0004.

canonical_claim: After costs, the average actively managed dollar underperforms the average passively managed dollar.
recommended_action: Keep both and record the before/after-costs scope on each; flagging them as contested would be a false positive.
synthesis: 0001 and 0002 look opposed — one says equal, the other says less — but they are scoped to before and after costs and are jointly asserted by the same author. 0006 supplies the mechanism (active managers trade frequently, which costs money) and 0003 scopes both to any time period.

canonical_claim: Passive and active investors are defined by whether the portfolio mirrors the market.
recommended_action: Store as definitions and link both as premises of the arithmetic claim.
synthesis: A complementary pair of definitions: 0004 fixes passive as holding every security in market proportion, 0005 defines active as its complement. Neither is evidence for the other; together they are the terms the whole argument depends on, which is why the argument is stated as conditional on them being defined sensibly.
